summary: Bolivia sorts passports into three groups: Group 1 — most of the EU, the UK, the United States, most of the Americas and a number of others — enters visa-free for up to 90 days a year; Group 2 pays for a tourist visa, obtainable on arrival or at a consulate; Group 3 needs a consular visa.

AF.notes: Group 3 nationality: Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG) lists it among the countries that need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, processing time or permitted stay, so ask a Bolivian consulate.

AL.notes: Group 2 nationality — a paid tourist visa, obtainable on arrival at a main airport or land border, or in advance at a consulate. On arrival it costs 300 UFV (about Bs 1,005 in October 2026), paid at Banco Unión after the officer authorizes it; stays total up to 90 days per calendar year.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months on arrival. Bolivian officials are strict about damaged passports and about visa pages being intact.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required if you arrive from or have transited a country with risk of transmission. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also lists a valid yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist visa or stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. Vaccination is strongly recommended — and sometimes checked on domestic flights — before traveling to the lowland departments of Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija or the Yungas.

source.name: Dirección General de Migración — Autorización de Ingreso por Turismo o Visita (tourist visa requirements, cost and processing)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Bolivia. The UK Foreign Office says the public health system is overstretched, private clinics in the main cities work with international insurance, and it is very important to have travel insurance and access to funds because you will need to pay up front for treatment.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bolivia travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must show a travel itinerary or return ticket, an invitation from a person legally resident in Bolivia registered with the Migration Directorate, or a hotel booking. Airlines may also check for an onward ticket at check-in.

source.name: Dirección General de Migración — Autorización de Ingreso por Turismo o Visita (tourist visa requirements, cost and processing)

proofOfFunds.text: Group 2 tourist-visa applicants must prove economic solvency with a sworn declaration backed by documents, such as recent bank statements. No minimum sum is published, and none is set for visa-free visitors.

source.name: Dirección General de Migración — Autorización de Ingreso por Turismo o Visita (tourist visa requirements, cost and processing)

declarations.name: Customs declaration
declarations.text: Before entering or leaving Bolivia, travelers fill in customs Form 250, a sworn declaration of new goods carried in accompanied baggage (on entry) and of currency (on entry and exit). It is available pre-printed or electronically.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

currencyLimits.text: Currency between USD 10,000 and USD 50,000 must be declared on entry, and between USD 10,000 and USD 20,000 on exit, on Form 250. Larger sums must be moved through a financial institution regulated by ASFI. Customs withholds 30% of undeclared currency, and of any amount above the limits.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export any item the Bolivian government considers a national treasure (patrimonio cultural) — including pre-Columbian artifacts, historical paintings, colonial-era items, native textiles, flora, fauna and fossils — without written permission from the Ministry of Culture.
Canada's travel advice notes that it is illegal to import coca leaves and related products into Canada; check the rules of your next destination before carrying any.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit and debit cards are not widely accepted outside urban centres and recommends carrying small notes for everyday costs such as street food, taxis and tips. It also says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange, so bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. The UK government says Bolivia is going through an economic crisis and a dollar shortage.

safety.text: Bolivia needs care with altitude, road travel and protests: a State of Emergency is in force over roadblocks, which can close highways at short notice, and the UK advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba. Express kidnapping and criminals posing as police are a risk, and taxi robberies have risen in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque — order radio taxis by phone.

bestTimeToVisit.text: The UK government's travel advice describes May to October as the dry season and November to March as the rainy season, when floods and landslides can block roads for days, particularly in mountainous areas. It also notes forest fires during the dry season in parts of southern and eastern Bolivia.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says you are at risk of high-altitude illness above 2,500 metres, naming La Paz (3,640 m), Uyuni (3,656 m), Oruro (3,735 m) and Potosí (4,090 m), and that the risk is higher if you ascend quickly or exercise or drink alcohol before acclimatising. High-altitude illness can be fatal.

Canada's travel advice says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange in Bolivia and to bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. Migration fees are set in UFV and paid at Banco Unión, not in cash at the counter.

The UK government's travel advice says protest groups often block roads without warning, that you should not try to cross blockades, and that recent blockades have caused fuel and fresh-food shortages in some areas. Canada's advice says roadblocks are common throughout the country.
The visa-free allowance is 90 days within a calendar year, not per entry. Leaving and coming back does not reset it, and overstays are fined per day on departure.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bolivia?
faq.answer: It depends on which of Bolivia's three groups your passport falls into. Group 1 — most EU and Schengen states, the UK, the United States, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Turkey, Russia, Australia, New Zealand and most of Latin America — needs no visa and gets up to 90 days a year. Group 2 pays for a tourist visa that can be issued on arrival or at a consulate. Group 3 needs a consular visa from a Bolivian consulate.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Bolivia?
faq.answer: No. Since Supreme Decree 5497 of 1 December 2025, US passport holders are in Group 1 and no longer need a consular visa or entry authorization to visit Bolivia as tourists — the former USD 160 visa no longer applies. Stays count toward the 90-day annual limit for visa-free visitors.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Bolivia?
faq.answer: Ninety days within a calendar year for visa-free visitors. Entry stamps often give 30 days initially. Check what you were granted and request more time, up to the 90-day annual cap, at a Dirección General de Migración office in any major city; the Directorate lists a fee of 250 UFV per period of up to 30 days.

faq.question: Can I really get a Bolivian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Group 2 nationalities can, at La Paz (El Alto), Santa Cruz (Viru Viru) and the main land borders. Bring a passport valid for at least six months, a recent 4x4 cm photo on a white background, a travel itinerary or return ticket (or a registered invitation letter or hotel booking), documents backing a sworn statement of your funds, a yellow fever certificate if you will visit high-risk areas, and the fee of 300 UFV, paid at Banco Unión once the officer authorizes it. Processing takes up to 10 minutes at border and airport posts, and up to 30 minutes at a migration office. Applying at a consulate first is slower but avoids surprises at a remote border post.

faq.question: What is Group 3?
faq.answer: Group 3 is the list of nationalities that, according to Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG), need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, how long a consulate takes or the permitted stay, so ask a Bolivian consulate well before you plan to travel. Group lists are revised by decree.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Bolivia?
faq.answer: It is required if you arrive from or have transited a yellow fever risk country, and Bolivia's Migration Directorate asks for a valid certificate with a tourist visa or stay application if you will visit high-risk endemic areas. Even if you are exempt, vaccination is strongly recommended before visiting the lowlands — Santa Cruz, Beni, Pando, Tarija and the Yungas — and is occasionally checked on domestic flights.
